stories.title: Ford nears completion of $2B factory overhaul for Fathom EV truck
stories.summary: Ford is on track to complete a $2 billion overhaul of a factory to build its Fathom EV truck, TechCrunch reports. The Verge adds that the truck is expected to carry a roughly $28,000 price tag as it nears production.
stories.whyItMatters: The project tests whether a legacy automaker can retool manufacturing to deliver an affordable EV profitably at a moment when EV demand growth has cooled.
whatToWatch: Confirmation of the factory overhaul's completion date
Official pricing and specs at launch
Production ramp timeline for the Fathom truck
questions: Will the roughly $28,000 price hold once the truck reaches production?
How much of the $2 billion investment depends on EV incentives staying in place?

stories.title: Flock adds safeguards to police cameras, but experts doubt it solves the misuse problem
stories.summary: Flock Safety is rolling out changes intended to make its license-plate-reading camera network harder for police officers to misuse, according to Engadget. But Ars Technica reports experts are skeptical the company can "tech its way out" of what they describe as a deeper, ongoing pattern of officers misusing the system to track people.
stories.whyItMatters: Flock's cameras are deployed widely across U.S. police departments, so how the company responds to misuse allegations will shape the broader fight over surveillance-tech accountability.
whatToWatch: Whether police departments adopt the new safeguards
Any newly reported misuse cases
Possible legislative or regulatory scrutiny of license-plate camera networks
questions: Can policy and oversight changes, rather than software tweaks, actually curb misuse?

stories.title: Instagram's redesigned wordmark draws backlash as 'AI slop'

stories.whyItMatters: Brand changes at platforms with billions of users draw outsized scrutiny, and the criticism reflects a wider backlash against AI-influenced design choices from big tech companies.
whatToWatch: Whether Meta responds to the design criticism
Whether other major apps follow with similar rebrands
questions: Is the backlash really about this specific design, or broader fatigue with AI-generated aesthetics?
